subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: In the number 58.36, what is the value of the digit 3?
questions.explain: The 3 sits in the first column after the decimal point, the tenths column, so it is worth 3 tenths = 0.3.

questions.q: Which number is exactly ten times bigger than 4.7?
questions.explain: Multiplying by 10 shifts every digit one column to the left, so 4.7 becomes 47.

questions.q: Which statement is TRUE?
questions.explain: Compare the tenths first: 0.7 has 7 tenths, 0.65 has 6 tenths, so 0.7 > 0.65. More digits does not mean bigger.

questions.q: Put these in order from smallest to largest: -3, 0, -7, 2.
questions.explain: On the number line the further left, the smaller. -7 is furthest left, then -3, then 0, then 2.

questions.q: Which of these numbers is prime?
questions.explain: 17 has exactly two factors (1 and 17). 1 has only one factor so is not prime, 9 = 3x3, and 21 = 3x7.

questions.q: Which number is a common multiple of both 3 and 5?
questions.explain: 15 is in the 3 times-table (3x5) and the 5 times-table (5x3), so it is a multiple of both.

questions.q: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 18 and 24?
questions.explain: 18 = 2x3x3 and 24 = 2x2x2x3. The shared primes are 2 and 3, so HCF = 2x3 = 6.

questions.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
questions.explain: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24... Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24... The first shared multiple is 24.

questions.q: Work out -4 - (-9).
questions.explain: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: -4 - (-9) = -4 + 9 = 5.

questions.q: Work out (-6) x (-3).
questions.explain: Two negative signs multiplied together give a positive answer: 6 x 3 = 18, so (-6) x (-3) = +18.

questions.q: Work out 5 + 2 x 3.
questions.explain: BIDMAS: do multiplication before addition. 2 x 3 = 6, then 5 + 6 = 11 (not 5+2=7 then x3).

questions.q: Work out (4 + 2)^2.
questions.explain: Brackets first: 4 + 2 = 6. Then the index: 6^2 = 36.

questions.q: What is 3 squared (3^2)?
questions.explain: 3 squared means 3 x 3 = 9. It does NOT mean 3 x 2 = 6.

questions.q: What is the square root of 49?
questions.explain: The square root undoes squaring. Since 7 x 7 = 49, the square root of 49 is 7.

questions.q: Which is 6300 written correctly in standard form?
questions.explain: Standard form is A x 10^n with A between 1 and 10. 6300 = 6.3 x 1000 = 6.3 x 10^3.

questions.q: What is 3/4 written as a decimal?
questions.explain: Divide the top by the bottom: 3 / 4 = 0.75. It is a terminating decimal.

questions.q: Work out 20% of £60.
Round 6.748 to 1 decimal place.
questions.explain: Look at the second decimal digit, 4. Since 4 is less than 5, the 7 stays the same, giving 6.7.

questions.q: Estimate 41 x 19 by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.
questions.explain: Round to 1 s.f.: 41 becomes 40 and 19 becomes 20. Then 40 x 20 = 800.

questions.q: A stick is measured as 8 cm to the nearest centimetre. What is the smallest length it could really be?
questions.explain: To the nearest cm, the true length lies within half a unit either side: from 7.5 cm up to 8.5 cm. The smallest is 7.5 cm.
